elements.name: html_introduction
elements.html:
Introduction

Biosphere reserves are areas of terrestrial and coastal/marine ecosystems, or a combination thereof, which are internationally recognized within the framework of UNESCO's Programme on Man and the Biosphere (MAB) They are established to promote and demonstrate a balanced relationship between humans and the biosphere. Biosphere reserves are designated by the International Coordinating Council of the MAB Programme at the request of the State concerned. Individual biosphere reserves remain under the sovereign jurisdiction of the State where they are situated. Collectively, all biosphere reserves form a World Network in which participation by States is voluntary.


The World Network is governed by the Statutory Framework adopted by the UNESCO General Conference in 1995 which presents the definition, objectives, criteria and the designation procedure for biosphere reserves. The actions recommended for the implementation of biosphere reserves are set out in the "Seville Strategy" and were further developed in the Madrid Action Plan (2008-2013). These documents should be used as basic references for the completion of this nomination form.

Use of Information

The information presented in this nomination form will be used by UNESCO:


  1. For examination of the biosphere reserve by the International Advisory Committee for Biosphere Reserves and by the Bureau of the MAB International Coordinating Council;
  2. To update communication and public information platforms, including the UNESCO website;
  3. To conduct analysis and reporting on the World Network of Biosphere reserves.

How to use this form

This form consists of multiple sections that are listed in the content menu on the left of the screen. When filling in the form, you may complete the sections and questions in any order. The bar at the top of each section will help you keep track of your progress.


The form content will adapt based on your input and provide feedback, such as warning or error messages, if information is missing or formatting rules are not observed. Questions that require specific information or response formats will contain instructions that you can read by clicking the “i” icon to the right of the question. Character limits and other formatting requirements will be listed below the response field.


While drafting the form, you may leave comments for other contributors by clicking on the comment icon that appears to the right of a question when you mouse over it. Comments will only be visible to contributors during the drafting phase and will be deleted once the form is submitted for review.


You may stop filling in the form at any time and come back to it later. Updates to the form are automatically saved, and you may also manually save your progress by clicking on the button at the bottom right of the screen. You can reopen the form from the Submission Dashboard of your user account and continue editing it at any time, provided the form has not been submitted for review and the deadline for submission has not passed.


Remember that the form must be submitted by a member of the UNESCO National Commission of your country before the 30 September submission deadline for the site to be considered for designation the following year.

elements.name: question1
elements.html:
A. Biosphere reserve profile

The information provided in this section will be used to update the public profile of the transboundary biosphere reserve, including on the UNESCO website and the Biodiversity Portal. This information can be updated any time outside the regular periodic review cycle. Updated information will be submitted to the Man and the Biosphere Programme Secretariat for review before it is published.

templateElements.title: D.02.3.4. Relevant international targets/ goals
choices: Goal 1. End poverty in all its forms everywhere
Goal 2. End hunger, achieve food security and improved nutrition and promote sustainable agriculture
Goal 3. Ensure healthy lives and promote well-being for all at all ages
Goal 4. Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all
Goal 5. Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls
Goal 6. Ensure availability and sustainable management of water and sanitation for all
Goal 7. Ensure access to affordable, reliable, sustainable and modern energy for all
Goal 8. Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all
Goal 9. Build resilient infrastructure, promote inclusive and sustainable industrialization and foster innovation
Goal 10. Reduce inequality within and among countries
Goal 11. Make cities and human settlements inclusive, safe, resilient and sustainable
Goal 12. Ensure sustainable consumption and production patterns
Goal 13. Take urgent action to combat climate change and its impacts
Goal 14. Conserve and sustainably use the oceans, seas and marine resources for sustainable development
Goal 15. Protect, restore and promote sustainable use of terrestrial ecosystems, sustainably manage forests, combat desertification, and halt and reverse land degradation and halt biodiversity loss
Goal 16. Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels
Goal 17. Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the Global Partnership for Sustainable Development Finance

Goal 16. Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels
Goal 17. Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the Global Partnership for Sustainable Development Finance

elements.name: question2
elements.html:
Clicking the “Send to National Commission” button will lock the form from further editing and alert the National Commission for UNESCO (or the government body in charge of relations with UNESCO) that the nomination form is ready to submit to the MAB secretariat for technical review.


The nomination form can only be sent if all questions are answered. You will be notified of the empty fields that require a response. If there are any questions that you are unable to answer, please explain why in the response field.


Please note that the technical review cannot start until the National Commission for UNESCO or other government body submits the form. Submissions must be made before 30 September annually.
